source: Bill Ackman / Pershing Square Capital Management (PSCM) public process — quality screen only. Execution is Kevin Xu.

hierarchy.qualityCheck: Ackman-style: durable operating company, simple business, not going to zero, identifiable catalyst path
hierarchy.buyDecision: Kevin Xu: one name, vibes + support + catalyst, don't chase, sell +20–30% / before rumor is news
hierarchy.conflictRule: ALL-IN requires BOTH gates. Xu: one name, don't chase, support+catalyst. Ackman: quality ≥4/6. If both pass, holding through the Q or ~1 month+ is allowed when the quality thesis is 'own the business until the tape reprices.' Xu still vetoes chase/pennies/second name. 13F never authorizes a BUY.

hardProhibitions: Do not copy the 13F into the Agentic book
Do not hold 8–11 (or even 2) names because Pershing does
Do not use 13F confluence as a BUY
Do not stretch horizon to fair-value 12 months
Do not skip Xu chase/penny/options/margin filters because PSCM owns the name

checklist.prompt: Can you explain what they do in two sentences?
Is demand likely still there in 5–10 years (quality), even if we only hold days–weeks?
Listed operating company — not penny, crypto, options, or a story that can go to zero overnight?
Is there a near-term reason the tape can reprice (Q, product, attention) — not a 12-month DCF?
Worst case is an ugly gap (~20–25%), not zero?
Would a concentrated quality investor own the *business* (not the 2-day tape)?

scoring.use: Memo + ranking column. Soft input to wont_go_to_zero. Never a second scoring system that can override Xu PASS (chase/penny/no catalyst).
scoring.altaRequires: Xu Alta AND quality checklist ≥4/6. No all-in if either gate fails. Quality 2–3/6 = no all-in (Media max / usually cash). Quality 0–1/6 → cash.

pershing13F.use: Optional hunting ground + quality examples. Stale (~45d). Never BUY because it is on the list. Never PASS a Xu setup only because it is not on the list (HOOD, GME-early, scanner names).
